steps.explanationAfterStep: Boron is less electronegative than hydrogen, so the B–H bonding pair is ready to move to carbon as a hydride. The C=O π bond breaks to keep carbon at four bonds.
The alkoxide (propan-2-ol, pKa about 17) is a slightly stronger base than methoxide (methanol, about 15.5), and methanol is the solvent, so the alcohol forms.
Methoxide fills the empty p orbital of boron. MeOBH₃⁻ still has three B–H bonds, so one borohydride can reduce several ketones.

title: Sodium borohydride reduction
subtitle: Borohydride delivers hydride to acetone; methanol protonates the alkoxide
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 6

alcohol.caption: propan-2-ol + methoxide + borane
hintTiers: BH₃ has only six electrons around boron. Which species can give it a pair?
The methoxide oxygen gives a lone pair to boron's empty orbital. One arrow.
Methoxide oxygen lone pair → new O–B bond.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: That takes the proton straight back. Look for an atom with an empty orbital instead.

alkoxide.caption: alkoxide + borane + methanol
hintTiers: The alkoxide oxygen is a strong base. Which molecule in the flask has an O–H proton?
The alkoxide lone pair takes the O–H proton of methanol. The O–H bonding pair stays on methanol's oxygen. Two arrows.
Alkoxide oxygen lone pair → new O–H bond to methanol's proton; methanol's O–H bond → lone pair on its oxygen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: The alkoxide can bind BH₃, and in the flask it often does. Take the simpler path here: methanol, the solvent, protonates the alkoxide.
Methanol's carbon is not an electrophile: methoxide would be a very poor leaving group. The alkoxide acts as a base.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Good: the alkoxide takes methanol's proton. Where does the O–H bonding pair go?

reactants.caption: acetone + sodium borohydride + methanol
hintTiers: Which bond of BH₄⁻ holds the electrons, and which atom of acetone is electron-poor?
A B–H bonding pair becomes a new C–H bond to the carbonyl carbon. Carbon cannot keep five bonds, so the C=O π pair moves onto oxygen. Two arrows.
B–H bond → new C–H bond to the carbonyl carbon; C=O π bond → lone pair on oxygen.
reactants.learnerPrompt: Borohydride is the source of hydride. Draw its attack on acetone.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: The carbonyl oxygen is electron-rich. Hydride goes to the electron-poor carbonyl carbon.
Methanol is a weak nucleophile and barely adds without acid. The hydride of borohydride is the nucleophile here.
The C=O π electrons move towards oxygen, the electronegative atom, not onto carbon.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right: hydride attacks the carbonyl carbon. But that carbon now has five bonds. Where do the C=O π electrons go?

mechanismSummary: A B–H bond of borohydride delivers hydride to the carbonyl carbon, and the C=O π electrons move onto oxygen. Methanol protonates the alkoxide, giving propan-2-ol, and the methoxide formed fills the empty orbital of BH₃.
